page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 physical cores hyperthreaded to 16 vCPUs with burstable CPU allocation. System memory consists of 32.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor cache hierarchy integrates 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. Hardware capabilities include Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel AMX matrix acceleration primitives (amx_tile and amx_int8), alongside VAES and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware extensions. This instance provides no local NVMe storage, relying exclusively on network-attached block storage, and operates with a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance in single-core and text-centric operations. The c7i-flex.4xlarge achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 33.24 GB/sec, single-core Geekbench score of 2045.0, Geekbench text processing at 2607.0, and small-model LLM text generation at 289.46 tokens/sec. Multi-core compute benchmarks align with middle-range cohort averages, recording a multi-core stress-ng performance of 16105.87, a PassMark CPU score of 24806.62, and a multi-core Geekbench score of 12124.0. Large-block DDR5 memory bandwidth measures 97.49 GB/sec for uncached reads and 74.81 GB/sec for writes. The burstable vCPU architecture delivers cost-efficient resource density for workloads with variable utilization profiles, though sustained max-load compute execution is subject to performance throttling relative to fixed-performance c7i instances.

The hardware configuration and instruction set support make c7i-flex.4xlarge effective for general compute tasks, software build automation, text manipulation pipelines, microservices, and small-scale machine learning inference. Benchmarked operational throughput includes static web serving at 26.5 GB/sec and Redis key-value processing at 20.47 million SET operations per second.
